newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-JOHN PAUL JR. BREAKS LEG IN INDY 500 CRASH.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-JOHN PAUL JR. BREAKS LEG IN INDY 500 CRASH.

text.p: Veteran driver John Paul Jr. became the first driver injured during practice for this year's Indianapolis 500 when he broke his right leg after his Dallara racer spun out of control Friday and slammed head-on into the turn four wall.

The 37-year-old Florida resident was bidding to make his seventh start in the Indianapolis 500. Paul made his first appearance at the Brickyard in 1985 and he started every Indy 500 in the 1990s except the 1995 race.
Paul, whose 10th place finish in 1992 was his best Indy showing, currently drives for PDM Racing.

On the track, practice continues with veterans and rookies getting for Saturday's pole qualifying session. Arie Luyendyk, the 1990 Indy 500 champion, heads into the qualifying session as the favourite after leading all three days of open practice.
Luyendyk's lap of 220.297 miles per hour (354.5 kph) from Wednesday's session is thus far the fastest.

Last year, the Dutchman set turned the fastest qualifying lap in the old model cars at 237.498 mph (382.2 kph). His 1990 championship was the fastest race in history with an average speed of 185.984 mph (299.3 kph).
Other pole favourites include Tony Stewart and Robby Gordon, who have been fast in practice this week and in testing before the Brickyard opened for pre-race practice.
The Indy 500 is planned for 200 laps around the 2.5-mile (4 km) oval on May 25.
